content_voiceover: Let's look at the irregular antibodies most commonly detected in Taiwan, since this is a favorite board question for local practice. Anti-Mia tops the list, followed by anti-E, anti-E plus c, anti-C, and anti-e — together these five make up about sixty percent of all irregular antibodies found here. The key reason is population genetics. Anti-Mia is essentially unique to Asian populations and reflects the Miltenberger blood group system, which most Western antibody panels don't even screen for well. Meanwhile the Rh antibodies, E, C, and e, are common because the E antigen positivity rate in Taiwan is around fifty percent, quite different from Caucasian populations. Interestingly, even though anti-Mia is the single most common antibody, the Mia-positive rate in Taiwan is only about seven point three percent, so finding compatible blood is usually not too difficult. Other less common but still notable antibodies include anti-Jka, anti-Lea, and anti-M. For boards, remember anti-Mia as the antibody almost unique to Chinese and Taiwanese populations, and know that Rh antibodies dominate the rest of the list.

Despite being most common, Mia antigen positivity is only about seven percent, so compatible blood is usually easy to find.

keypoint_voiceover: For your exam, remember five things. Anti-Mia is the top irregular antibody in Taiwan and is nearly unique to Asian populations. Anti-Mia plus the Rh antibodies anti-E, anti-C, and anti-e account for roughly sixty percent of all irregular antibodies detected locally. Taiwan's E antigen positivity rate is about fifty percent, which explains why Rh antibodies are so common. Even though Mia is the most frequent antibody, its antigen positivity is only about seven percent, so compatible units are usually easy to find. And don't forget anti-Jka, anti-Lea, and anti-M as the next tier of common antibodies.
